cells: Hot material rises and cooler material sinks, creating circulation.
Gravity pushes plates away from elevated ridges.
Dense subducting plate pulls the rest downward.

blocks.content: The heat within the Earth generates convection currents that cause the overlying lithospheric plates to move.

rows: Sinking of cold, dense subducting plate pulls the rest of the trailing lithosphere downward due to gravity.
Gravitational force pushes elevated, warm, buoyant crust away from the ridge crest.
Thermal upwelling and downwelling within the mantle drag overlying plates horizontally.

items: Arthur Holmes is frequently tested as the scientist who postulated the Convection Current Theory in the 1930s.
Slab pull is recognized as the dominant driving force in plate motion compared to ridge push and mantle traction.
The asthenosphere (part of the upper mantle) is the ductile layer enabling lithospheric plate mobility.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Arthur Holmes in the 1930s proposed that thermal convection currents operating in the mantle drive plate movement.
Mantle convection currents are generated by heat originating from radioactive decay and primordial heat within the Earth.
Rigid lithospheric plates float horizontally over the weak, ductile, semi-molten asthenosphere.
The primary forces propelling plate motion are Slab Pull at convergent subduction zones and Ridge Push at divergent ridges.
